reports.title: ConocoPhillips announces third-quarter 2026 results and increases quarterly ordinary dividend by 11%

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: Fourth-quarter 2026 production is expected to be 2.32 to 2.36 million barrels of oil equivalent per day. Full-year capital expenditures and adjusted operating cost guidance remain unchanged. Additional guidance items can be found on slide 11 of the company’s third-quarter 2026 earnings presentation, available on the company’s investor relations website.

ConocoPhillips will host a conference call today at 12:00 p.m. Eastern time to discuss this announcement. To listen to the call and view related presentation materials and supplemental information, go to www.conocophillips.com/investor. A recording and transcript of the call will be posted afterward.

desk.headline: Adjusted EPS doubled to $3.27 on higher prices, beat; dividend up 11%, full-year spending guidance unchanged
results: Net profit rose to $4.0bn ($3.34 a share) from $1.7bn; adjusted EPS was $3.27 against $1.61, helped by a tax-reserve reversal in the GAAP figure.
Higher oil and gas prices did the work: the average realised price rose 32% to $61.40 per barrel of oil equivalent.
Output fell 4% to 2,302 MBOED (2% on an underlying basis) as Lower 48 growth was outweighed by the Middle East conflict's hit to Qatar and higher Surmont royalties.
Cash from operations was $7.2bn and free cash flow about $4.0bn; $1.6bn more came in from selling non-core assets.
$3.4bn returned to shareholders ($2.4bn buybacks); quarterly dividend raised 11% to $0.93, payable 1 Dec 2026.

guidance.summary: Full-year capital spending and adjusted operating cost guidance are unchanged. Fourth-quarter production is guided at 2.32–2.36 million boe a day.

points: Early 2027 view: capital spending modestly lower, low-single-digit underlying production growth led by the Lower 48, and lower unit operating costs.
Qatar output improved from the second quarter but is still below pre-conflict levels; the next Qatar LNG train (NFE) is expected in the first half of 2027.
The company aims to return 45% of operating cash flow again in 2027, with buybacks expected to step up in the fourth quarter.
Willow in Alaska is past halfway with first oil still targeted for early 2029; the $5bn asset-sale programme is complete.
An unsolicited offer for the Norway business is being evaluated with no decision made; cost inflation in fuel, logistics and chemicals is being offset by efficiencies.
call.source: Call transcript: The Motley Fool, 5 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Qatar volumes return to pre-conflict levels and NFE starts on time in 1H 2027.
The formal 2027 capital and production plan versus the early indications.
